definitions.explanation: A small, narrow street or pathway, especially in traditional neighborhoods or historic districts. Often appears in place names throughout Japan, particularly in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {小路|こうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: I walk along the narrow lane.
The narrow lanes in the old town have charm.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{小路|こうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{散歩|さんぽ}している→散歩する：26840_sanposuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{思|おも}いがけず{素敵|すてき}な⟦お{店|みせ}→お店：21164_omise⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つける→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: When strolling through Kyoto's narrow lanes, you can unexpectedly discover charming shops.

notes:
USAGE: {小路|こうじ} refers to narrow streets or lanes, especially in traditional or historic areas. It frequently appears in place names, particularly in Kyoto (e.g., {先斗町|ぽんとちょう}{小路|こうじ}).

Also read as こみち, which has a more poetic or literary feel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{路地|ろじ}→路地：06501_roji⟧{小路|こうじ}: narrow back streets and lanes
- {裏|うら}{小路|こうじ}: back lane, back alley
- {小路|こうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}ける→抜ける：02385_nukeru⟧: to pass through an alley

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {小路|こうじ}: narrow lane (often in place names)
- ⟦{路地|ろじ}→路地：06501_roji⟧: alley, back street (narrower, between buildings)
- ⟦{横丁|よこちょう}→横丁：18976_yokochou⟧: side street, alley (often lined with shops or bars)
